guideTitle: Best Leaf Vacuums for Wet Leaves (2026)
metaTitle: Best Leaf Vacuums for Wet Leaves in 2026
metaDescription: Six leaf vacuums compared for damp and wet leaves by impeller, anti-clog design, bag size and power source, so soggy leaves collect instead of jamming.
expertTake: The EGO LV5000 is the best choice for damp leaves because its six-blade metal impeller shreds sticky material that jams plastic ones, but you must supply EGO batteries. The Greenworks 40V is the value pick with battery and charger included. Skip the whole idea of vacuuming soaked leaves: every handheld here jams or overloads on a truly saturated pile, so let them drain first.
introParagraphs: Wet leaves are the toughest material a leaf vacuum can be asked to swallow. Water adds weight and stickiness, so leaves cling to the tube walls, pack into the impeller housing and form a paste that stalls a weak motor.

The sensible approach is to treat damp, not soaked, leaves as the realistic limit. Look for an impeller that cuts rather than smears, a smooth wide tube and enough motor torque to push through the load, and expect to stop and clear jams occasionally.

products.name: EGO Power+ LV5000 vacuum mulcher, 500 CFM, 16:1, tool only

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Tool only, no battery or charger

products.description:
Damp leaves punish plastic impellers because they stick to the blades and smear instead of cutting. The LV5000's six-blade metal impeller slices through them, which is the reason it tops this guide. A 16 to 1 ratio is the highest of the cordless units here, and a heavy-duty 40 liter bag is described as easy to empty.

The cost is the entry fee. It is sold as tool only, with no battery or charger, so a buyer with no EGO packs must budget for both. For an existing EGO owner it is among the best additions to the garage, since the same pack runs the mower and trimmer. The blower side at 500 CFM is modest, but wet leaves are a vacuum job.

Metal impellers are tough but still need care: clear the chamber after every wet session, rinse sap off the blades with a hose with the pack removed, and let it dry fully. A stalled impeller is a signal to stop, not to push harder. Remove the battery before you reach into the chamber, because a metal impeller will not forgive a finger, and keep a stiff plastic scraper in the shed for cleaning the housing.
products.bestFor: EGO battery owners who want the toughest cutting action for damp leaves.
pros: Six-blade metal impeller cuts sticky leaves
16:1 mulch ratio is strong for a cordless
Packs shared across the EGO line
cons: A full wet bag is heavy

products.name: Greenworks 48V (24V x 2) vacuum, 520 CFM, 240 MPH, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
For wet leaves, torque matters more than top speed, and the Greenworks pairs a brushless motor with two 24V packs working together as 48V. The maker describes it as blasting stubborn wet leaves with 240 MPH, and that jet speed also helps in blower mode to peel leaves off the ground before you vacuum them. Two 4.0Ah batteries and a dual-port charger are in the box.

What the listing does not tell you is the impeller material or the mulch ratio, so treat it as a strong motor driving a standard design. Against the EGO LV5000 it has more blower power but a less proven cutting system. Against the 40V Greenworks it has more speed and a second pack.

Wet work is hard on the packs, so rotate them and let each cool before charging. Clean the chamber after use, and keep the tube joints dry so they do not corrode.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a complete cordless kit for mixed damp and dry leaves.

products.name: SuperHandy 7 HP 209cc gas leaf vacuum and chipper, 6 bushel bag
products.description:
A 209cc overhead-valve engine is the only power source here that can keep up with really heavy wet leaves, since torque on a lawnmower-class engine does not sag the way a battery does. The 6 bushel bag swallows a lot of damp material before you stop, and castor wheels spare you from carrying the machine.

Its 10 to 1 mulch ratio is lower than the cordless units, but the capacity of the bag and the power behind the impeller make it work in conditions where a handheld would stall. It doubles as a wood chipper, which is useful if the same yard also produces branches.

It is a heavy, noisy machine with real upkeep: engine oil, air filter and spark plug on a schedule, fresh fuel, and storage space. Clear the intake and impeller with the engine off before you reach in, and wash wet leaf paste out of the chamber after each session. Check the tyre pressure on the wheels and the belt or clutch guard as part of the seasonal service, since vibration from a wet load works fasteners loose faster than dry work does.
products.bestFor: Large properties with heavy wet leaf loads.
pros: 209cc engine holds torque under wet load
cons: Heavy, loud and needs engine upkeep

products.name: Greenworks 40V blower vacuum, 505 CFM, 12:1, 5.0Ah battery
products.description:
The 40V Greenworks is the budget route to a capable cordless vacuum, with a brushless motor that the maker says delivers twice the torque and longer runtime. A turbo button gives 185 MPH on demand, and a variable speed dial lets you ease off for damp, light leaves. The 5.0Ah battery and charger are in the box.

On wet leaves its strength is also its limit: one 5.0Ah pack is the only fuel, so a long wet session needs a second pack. The 12 to 1 mulch ratio is average, and for sticky leaves expect a lower real figure. It sits below the 48V Greenworks in speed and below the EGO LV5000 in build.

Store the battery indoors, clean the chamber after each use and watch for sap on the impeller. A wiped blade makes the next session smoother. Because this kit has one pack, plan the work so the wettest patches are done first while the battery is full, and leave the lighter, drier areas for the end.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a complete cordless kit for light-to-damp leaves.
cons: One battery limits long wet jobs

products.name: MZK 40V brushless leaf vacuum mulcher, 700 CFM, 40L bag

specList.label: Design
specList.value: Internal suction tube with square connector

products.description:
MZK's selling point for wet leaves is the anti-jam design: an internal suction tube and a square connector are meant to remove the joint where damp leaves usually hang up. A brushless motor drives 700 CFM, and four adjustable speeds let you meter power into wetter material.

The 700 CFM peak comes with a 10 second turbo, so do not expect it for a whole session. The listing does not clarify what battery ships, so confirm that before buying. Against the Greenworks 40V it has far more claimed airflow, but less certainty about the kit.

Sticky leaves collect at the square connector first, so check it after every session. Keep the pack at partial charge and store the unit with the bag removed. Squeeze the square connector clean with a gloved hand at the start of each session, since a small bridge of packed leaf there is how most jams begin.
products.bestFor: Damp leaves where jam resistance matters most.
pros: Internal tube to reduce joint clogging

products.name: RYOBI 40V HP brushless vacuum mulcher, 600 CFM, 100 MPH, tool only
products.description:
RYOBI's single-tube design is a real asset for damp leaves, because one smooth tube for blowing, vacuuming and mulching means fewer joints for sticky leaves to catch on. A jet fan design produces 600 CFM, which gives the suction volume to pull heavy leaves, and the 40V HP system is described as delivering high power.

The 100 MPH speed is low, so it will not peel leaves off turf as well as the Greenworks 48V at 240 MPH. Use it on leaves that sit loosely on the surface rather than ones glued to the lawn. It is sold tool only with a bag, so you need 40V RYOBI packs.

The usual care applies: rinse the tube with the pack out, hang the bag to dry and check the zipper for grit. A clean smooth tube is the reason this design works, so do not store the machine with leaf paste dried on the inside. A quick rinse with a hose, with the battery removed, saves a stubborn scrub in spring.
products.bestFor: RYOBI 40V owners picking up damp leaves from hard surfaces and loose lawn.
pros: Single smooth tube means fewer clog points
cons: 100 MPH is slow for stuck wet leaves

buyingCriteria.explanation: Wet leaves stick to blades and smear instead of slicing. A metal six-blade impeller like the EGO LV5000's cuts through them, while a plastic one often clogs. If your leaves are damp for most of the season, choose metal.
Sticky leaves catch on joints and ridges. RYOBI's single smooth tube and MZK's internal anti-jam tube reduce those catch points. A tube that has to be swapped between modes has more places to jam.

A stalled impeller is the main failure with wet leaves. Brushless motors and gas engines hold torque under load, so the Greenworks 48V and the SuperHandy 209cc are less likely to bog. Do not judge on MPH alone.

Wet leaves weigh several times what dry ones do, so a full 40 liter bag on a shoulder strap gets heavy fast. The SuperHandy's 6 bushel bag sits on wheels. For a handheld, plan to empty the bag when it is half full.

Quoted ratios are for dry leaves. Wet leaves shred less well, so expect a lower reduction than the 16:1 EGO or 12:1 Greenworks figures. Do not choose on the ratio alone, and be sceptical of any machine that quotes a number without saying what leaves it was measured on.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Battery or fuel for a long job
buyingCriteria.explanation: Wet work is hard on batteries. A single 5.0Ah pack in the Greenworks 40V kit will not last a long soggy session, while a gas SuperHandy runs until the tank is empty. Plan a second pack for any cordless unit, and treat a quoted runtime as a dry-leaf figure that wet loads cut roughly in half.

specDecoder.meaning: The number and material of the chopping blades. Metal and more blades handle sticky material better.
specDecoder.watchFor: EGO's six metal blades versus the unspecified blades on most rivals.

specDecoder.meaning: Air volume in blower mode, a rough proxy for suction volume.
Volume reduction quoted on dry leaves. Wet leaves will reduce less.
Brushless motors hold torque under load and run cooler. That matters when leaves resist.
A bushel is about 35 liters, so 6 bushels is around 210 liters of bag. It sets how often you stop.
specDecoder.watchFor: SuperHandy's 6 bushel bag against 40 liter handheld bags.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting and clog resistance
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated impeller material, tube design and anti-jam features. The EGO's metal blades, the RYOBI single tube and the MZK internal tube scored highest. Designs with extra joints were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Torque under load
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet, we favoured brushless motors and the gas 209cc engine. Wet leaves stall weak motors, so torque matters more than speed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bag capacity and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 40 liter bags to the SuperHandy's 6 bushel bag, and considered how heavy a wet bag becomes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and kit value
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted what ships in the box. The Greenworks kits include batteries while the EGO and RYOBI are tool only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered cleanup after wet work, sap on blades and corrosion in joints. Parts support was also weighed.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The Greenworks, EGO, MZK and RYOBI are quiet and light, but wet work drains packs and strains motors. They suit damp rather than soaked leaves.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The SuperHandy 209cc holds torque and carries a huge bag. It is loud, heavy and needs engine care. It suits large wet jobs.

howToChoose.note: Cordless for damp leaves on small to mid lots; gas for soggy, large properties.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A cutting impeller, a smooth wide tube and strong torque. Let leaves drain for a day if you can, and work in small handfuls. Stop and clear jams promptly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EGO LV5000 and the SuperHandy are best for sticky or heavy wet loads. The RYOBI and MZK handle damp leaves with fewer jams.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your yard is wet for much of the fall. The EGO's metal impeller or the SuperHandy's engine saves time and frustration.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Wet days are rare. The Greenworks 40V kit does the job without extra purchases.

maintenance.why: Wet leaf paste hardens on blades and unbalances them. Rinse it out with the pack removed.
Damp tubes corrode joints and bags mildew. Air dry fully before storage.
Sap and chips dull cutting edges. A dull impeller smears leaves.
Wet work is hard on cells. Let them cool before charging and store at partial charge.
Oil, filter and spark plug keep the SuperHandy running. Drain fuel for winter.

faq.q: Can a leaf vacuum handle wet leaves?
faq.a: Damp leaves, yes, but saturated piles jam most handhelds. Let them drain, work in small handfuls and keep the nozzle moving, because a nozzle held in one spot gulps a whole clump at once and chokes the tube. A metal impeller or a gas engine helps, and so does switching the machine off to empty the bag before it is completely full.
The Greenworks 40V kit sits at a low tier, the MZK and RYOBI in the middle, and the SuperHandy higher. Pay more for a cutting impeller or engine torque.

faq.q: Why does my vacuum keep clogging on wet leaves?
faq.a: Sticky leaves cling to joints and blades. A smooth tube, a metal impeller and a clean chamber reduce clogs. Stop and clear it rather than forcing.

faq.q: Is mulching wet leaves worth it?
faq.a: Yes as a volume cut, but wet leaves shred coarsely and the ratio is lower than quoted. Expect a wet, heavy mulch that breaks down quickly.

faq.q: Cordless or gas for wet leaves?
faq.a: Gas holds torque and capacity better on heavy loads. Cordless is quieter and easier for damp, modest jobs. Choose by the size of the lot.

faq.q: Do I need to dry leaves first?
faq.a: It helps a lot. Even a day of drainage lowers weight and stickiness. Dry leaves vacuum far better, so on a wet week the smartest move is often to spread a tarp, rake the leaves onto it and let them dry in the sun before the vacuum comes out. That one habit saves more wear on the machine than any feature on this list.
